source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's DFW2 campus in Lewisville, Texas publishes 12 MW of IT capacity across 200,000 square feet of technical space, and that 12 MW is the only power figure the operator makes public.

The pattern here is a published number with no published composition. There is no rack count, no accelerator count, no power usage effectiveness, and no tenant roster. Converting 12 MW into racks requires assuming a density: at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training figure, the load is roughly 300 racks, and at 10 kW per rack it is roughly 1,200. That arithmetic is an assumption about density, not a fact about this building, and the operator has not endorsed either number.

The certifications describe what workloads the campus is qualified to carry, not who occupies it. PCI DSS covers payment card data, HIPAA covers protected health information, ISO 27001 covers an information security management system, FISMA covers federal information systems, SSAE 16 Type II covers controls relevant to financial reporting, and TIA-942 covers telecommunications infrastructure design. None of them names a tenant.

Texas holds 137 mapped facilities, of which 19 publish a megawatt figure this site has read. Those 19 total 475.41 MW, and DFW2 ranks twelfth among them. The ranking is therefore a ranking within a minority of Texas facilities, since most mapped sites publish no figure at all. On the published numbers this is a mid-sized campus in the largest concentration of data centers mapped here, and its 12 MW is a small share of the state's published total. What the data does not cover is whether the campus is expanding, what hardware sits inside it, or how much of its capacity is under contract.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
